cr-impact.assumptions: The request is a to-do list: anybody adds a task, marks it done, and possibly edits or deletes it. It is persisted on the server, because system-states.md says the browser stores nothing. cr-requirements and cr-scenarios will take impact.md as today's state and will turn its "could not determine" list into questions. That list covers: keep or replace the guestbook; whether "odznaczenie" means a done task can be unticked; whether "ew." makes edit/delete optional; what fields a task has; seed data; the route and the `/` redirect; and simultaneous toggles.

history.note: cr-request Phase 5 takes the boundary baseline straight after `cr new`, but `cr new` leaves spec/changes/status.json stale, so the baseline is RED by construction on gate:Specification gates ("status.json is stale" -> generated-indexes + one-change-at-a-time); recorded as the skill says, that gate would ride as pre-existing red for the whole change. Worked around by running `sdd-engine gen_indexes` before re-taking the baseline, a step no skill names; cost two extra boundary runs (~5 min).

history.note: The signal definitions for contract_touched, schema_touched and screen_touched say "a named surface appears in api.md / data-model.md / ui/". Applied literally to a brand-new concept they find nothing, and would switch off design-api, design-data, design-ui and build-migration for a new feature. The worker had to read them as "the spec surfaces the change reaches" (the route register, "The only table", PageFrame navigation) before it could measure.
